name: talk
description: Voice mode: a spoken conversation with the assistant. It listens until the person stops speaking, writes what was said down on the computer that hosts the workspace, says back what it heard, sends it as their message, reads the reply aloud in a voice on this device, and listens again, every word shown in the chat as it goes. When replies are not read aloud it lets the microphone go and waits for Speak. Shown only where the browser can record and speech-to-text is on the host.

use.when: a person would rather talk than type: hands busy, eyes elsewhere, or speech easier than keys.
use.not: saying one message and reading it before it goes, which is Dictate (the voice component).
use.with: the chat, whose message and log it uses: everything said and answered is written there.

message.description: The id of the chat's message field, which the words go into and are sent from.

action.description: Where the sound is sent to be written down.

a11y.role: region named Voice mode, shown only where it can work, holding a start and end button, one button for the person's part of the turn that stays in place, a checkbox, a hint about headphones, and one status that says each change of state once

keyboard.does: reaches Start voice mode (End voice mode while it runs), then the turn button (Done speaking while listening, Skip the reply while reading, Speak when it waits), then Read replies aloud

keyboard.key: Enter or Space on the turn button
keyboard.does: ends the person's turn, skips the reply, or starts listening; its label changes in place, so the focus stays on it, and it goes back to the start button when voice mode pauses or ends
ends voice mode from anywhere on the page, stopping the microphone and the reading

wcag.notes: Everything said and every reply is written in the chat as it happens, so nothing is only heard (1.2). The microphone is asked for when Start voice mode is pressed and is off while a reply is read, so the assistant never hears itself. It is let go, so the browser's own sign goes out, whenever voice mode waits, pauses after 30 seconds with nothing heard, or ends; End voice mode or Escape stops it at once. What it is doing is said in words, once each time it changes, and shown beside the buttons, never by a colour or a moving picture alone (1.4.1, 2.2.2, 4.1.3). Hearing you is shown and not said, because a screen reader speaking while the person talks would be written down as their words. What was heard is said back as it is sent, so a wrong word is caught. When replies are not read aloud (a screen reader already reads them) it waits for Speak instead of listening while the reply is being read. One turn button changes its words in place, so the focus is never lost (2.4.3). Replies are read in a voice on this device only. Done speaking ends a turn by hand for anyone whose pauses are long (2.2.1).

machine.identify: data-state says what it is doing: off, listening, hearing, writing, answering, speaking, waiting or paused.
machine.operate: An agent has no microphone: write in the chat's message instead. data-action takes 16 kHz WAV and answers {"text": "..."}.
